extracted.intended_audience: Organizations and individuals applying for federal grants via Grants.gov (applicant teams, AORs, Workspace Owners, grant administrators, consultants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and using the Grants.gov Workspace workflow to prepare and submit federal grant applications, including choosing Basic/Intermediate/Advanced approaches, assigning roles, and collaborating on forms online or offline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace purpose and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Workspace is the standard way for organizations or individuals to apply for federal grants in Grants.gov. Workspace allows a grant team to simultaneously access and edit different forms within an application. Plus, the forms can be filled out online or offline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Workspace to enable multi-user collaboration on an application; choose between online and offline form completion depending on your team's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an application approach (Basic / Intermediate / Advanced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov Workspace allows applicants and organizations to choose which approach to use for their application workflow. Here are three approaches that applicants can take when completing a Workspace application: Basic, Intermediate, Advanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the approach that matches your organization's size, number of registered users, and collaboration needs (see individual approach descriptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic approach — suitability and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic: Best for organizations with 1-2 registered Grants.gov users. Application forms are downloaded and emailed to collaborators before being uploaded back to the workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Basic when a very small team handles the application and collaborators prefer working on downloaded forms and returning them via email for a single user to upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate approach — suitability and team roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediate: Best for organizations with 3-5 registered Grants.gov users. Applicant teams are typically comprised of an AOR who submits, as well as a Workspace Owner who oversees form completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Intermediate when you have a small team with distinct submission authority (AOR) and a Workspace Owner coordinating form completion across members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced approach — external collaborators and owner-managed access
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced: Best for organizations with external Grants.gov users, such as consultants. Workspace Owner manages form access. Workspace Owner adds subforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Advanced if you need to grant access to external consultants or complex subform management; assign a Workspace Owner to control access and subforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of custom roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations are also able to create custom roles and assign these roles to the users affiliated with their organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and assign custom roles when built-in roles do not match your internal workflow or privilege requirements; consult the Custom Roles guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan internal application workflow with provided resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference the following content when planning out your internal application workflow: Workspace Process Timeline (infographic), Workspace Roles and Access (resource explaining roles, privileges and access levels), Video: How to Create a Workspace, and a complete list of training videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the process timeline and roles/access infographic to identify decision points, map responsibilities (AOR, Workspace Owner, collaborators), and determine whether Basic/Intermediate/Advanced fits your organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace roles, privileges, and access levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Workspace Roles and Access: This resource explains the roles, privileges and access levels that can be used when completing a grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand each role's privileges before assigning users (who can edit, upload, submit, manage access, add subforms) to ensure proper separation of duties and secure workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration method: online vs. offline form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms can be filled out online or offline — your choice. In the Basic approach, forms are downloaded and emailed to collaborators before being uploaded back to the workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether collaborators will edit forms directly in Workspace or work on downloaded copies and consolidate edits; consider version control, convenience, and number of users when choosing.
